description: Folders that filecat recognises by their layout as a database server's data or a backup program's store, what it does with each, and what is known about them. The detection itself is code (module); this catalog is its reference, and filecat reads the measure thresholds (actions.measure_when) from it. tests/test_store_formats.py keeps the two in step. rollup_children lists the immediate sub-folders of a store (names or * wildcards) that a [BACKUP] or [DATABASE] rollup replaces when the store type is automatic or the store is listed in the config (docs/rollups.md section 4); an empty list means the format has no bulk folder to roll up. The "archives" and "archives_identified_only" lists sit beside it as reference only: file formats the probe lists (module and function named) or only identifies from freedesktop, with magic bytes, globs, a spec link and notes. No code reads them.

actions.list: Data file recorded from the directory listing only: name, size, created/modified times, kind 'data', probe.<data_tag> = <id>. Never opened.
actions.measure: Read, hashed and probed like any other file.
actions.summarize: When the walk finishes the folder, the module reads the program's own small metadata files and the folder's record gets probe.<summary_key>.
actions.virtual: Folder recorded with its summary but not walked: its files show data that lives elsewhere, and their sizes are not disk space.
actions.in_use: A data file the server holds open (Windows sharing or lock violation, WinError 32/33) when measured is recorded as probe.db_in_use instead of an error.

formats.name: PostgreSQL cluster data directory (PGDATA)

detection.description: A folder holding the PG_VERSION file and the base/ and global/ folders.

not_walked: pg_tblspc/<oid> (junctions to tablespaces, recorded as links)

metadata_read.global/pg_control: first 32 bytes: system identifier, pg_control and catalog versions, cluster state, time of last update (little-endian)
metadata_read.postmaster.pid: pid (line 1) and port (line 4); present while the server runs
metadata_read.base/<oid>/: one folder per database: file count, bytes, newest time
metadata_read.pg_tblspc/: tablespace OIDs and their link targets

measure_when.text: not modified for 90 days and at least 1 MiB

actions.enrich: measures listed files once they are quiet, re-checking the file just before reading; --force does not override

formats.instance_keys: pg:<system identifier> -- shared by copies of the cluster and by physical replicas
problems: global/pg_control missing or unreadable
pg_wal missing
pg_control says 'in production' but no postmaster.pid: a copy taken while the server ran, or a crash
notes: Relation files are 8 KB pages in 1 GB segments (<relfilenode>, .1, .2 ...; _fsm and _vm forks); a busy cluster has thousands of small ones, hence the 1 MiB floor.
Database names are in pg_database (global/1262) and are not read yet; databases are listed by OID, with oid 1 = template1.

formats.name: MySQL / MariaDB data directory (datadir)

detection.description: An InnoDB or Aria marker file plus the mysql system schema (folder, or mysql.ibd in 8.0+).

listed_only: every other top-level file not measured_normally

metadata_read.mysql_upgrade_info: version of the last upgrade (MariaDB, MySQL before 8.0)
metadata_read.<schema>/: table count from table file names (.ibd .frm .MYD/.MYI .MAD/.MAI .CSV .ARZ ...; #P# partitions folded), storage engines, bytes

measure_when.text: not modified for 90 days and at least 1 MiB

actions.enrich: measures listed files once they are quiet, re-checking the file just before reading; --force does not override

formats.instance_keys: mysql:<server-uuid> -- shared by copies of the datadir (a replica gets its own uuid)
notes: Flavor is MariaDB when aria_log_control exists or mysql_upgrade_info says MariaDB.
MySQL 8.0+ writes no plain version file; version_hint '8.0+' is given when mysql.ibd exists.
todo: MySQL 8 version from the .err log or mysql.ibd SDI
datadir from my.ini / my.cnf and the service command line

formats.name: MongoDB dbPath

detection.description: The WiredTiger version file plus MongoDB's catalog or storage.bson.

metadata_read.storage.bson: storage engine and options: directoryPerDB, directoryForIndexes, groupCollections
metadata_read.mongod.lock: size only: non-empty (holds the pid) while mongod runs, empty after a clean stop

measure_when.text: not modified for 90 days and at least 1 MiB

actions.enrich: measures listed files once they are quiet, re-checking the file just before reading; --force does not override

notes: mongod holds mongod.lock and WiredTiger.lock locked on Windows (reading them fails with a sharing violation), so they are listed, never opened.
Collection and index files are named collection-<n>-<number>.wt before 8.0 and collection-<uuid>.wt since.
WiredTigerHS.wt is the history store (4.4+); _tmp/spilldb/ is a second WiredTiger instance for spilled query data (8.0+).
Which namespace a .wt file holds is in _mdb_catalog.wt, not read yet; databases are named only with directoryPerDB.

examples.what: filecat's own catalog server, running: MongoDB 9.0.4 (from the folder), WiredTiger 12.0.0, flat layout (no directoryPerDB), 19 collections, 47 indexes, 2 journal files, 86 data files / 2.1 GiB; mongod.lock and WiredTiger.lock locked

todo: storage.dbPath from mongod.cfg and the service command line

formats.name: SQL Server database files

detection.except: an .mdf with an .mds of the same name beside it (Alcohol 120% disc image)
detection.description: Any folder holding a primary data file: instance DATA folders, LocalDB, App_Data, detached copies.

listed_only: *.ldf (directly in the folder; a subfolder with an .mdf is its own store)

metadata_read.path: instance from MSSQLnn[_nn].NAME (MSSQL16 = 2022, MSSQL10_50 = 2008 R2) or Microsoft SQL Server\<nnn>\ (170 = 2025)
metadata_read.*.mdf/*.ndf/*.ldf: size, modified time, quiet; data paired with its log by name (<db>_log.ldf, <db>.ldf, <db>log.ldf; system databases by their fixed names)

measure_when.text: not modified for 1 hour, any size

actions.enrich: measures listed files once they are quiet, re-checking the file just before reading; --force does not override

notes: An attached database's files are held open by the server, and its modified time can stay old while attached; measuring then records probe.db_in_use.
Logs often sit on another drive, so an .mdf without an .ldf beside it is normal.
Real example: C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\170\LocalDB\Binn\Templates (master, model, msdb templates) and Binn (mssqlsystemresource).
todo: database name, version and collation from the boot page (page 9) of quiet .mdf files
DefaultData / DefaultLog / BackupDirectory from the registry

formats.name: Synology Active Backup for Business destination

detection.description: The @ActiveBackup folder of a destination share.

metadata_read.@data/file_map.db: every volume image in the pool, with size
metadata_read.PC-<HOST>-<task>/config.json: host, OS, device UUID, task settings (the agent token is not copied)
metadata_read.PC-<HOST>-<task>/target.db: versions (status, times, UUID), objects, mount map

problems: failed versions (status 4)
volume images missing from the pool or stopped part way (.suspend)
small objects missing or of the wrong size
version folders target.db does not know
notes: The pool is ~32 MiB chunk buckets; listing a 1 TB pool takes about a minute instead of hours of reading.

formats.name: Synology ABB virtual view
notes: Every volume of every version appears as a full-size image served from the pool; its sizes are not disk space.

formats.name: Synology Hyper Backup target (.hbk)

detection.description: A <task>_<n>.hbk folder on a local share, USB disk, rsync server or Hyper Backup Vault.

metadata_read._Syno_TaskConfig: task name, source host and model, unikey, backed-up folders and apps, encryption, rotation (named fields only)
metadata_read.Config/version_info.db: every version: id, time, status, locked, shares, per-version file counts and sizes
metadata_read.last_status.conf: the last backup's start, end and version
every pool and index file with its size, checked against the walk's listing

actions.verify_flag: --verify-backups (reads every file Guard lists and compares its CRC32)

formats.machine_keys: source host name, the id at the front of the unikey
problems: files in Guard's manifest missing or of another size
versions with a failed status
errors in the last integrity check's log
with --verify-backups: files whose CRC32 differs from Guard's
notes: Synology does not document the format; the layout was read from Hyper Backup 4.2 targets (target_ver 0.3, index_ver 0.9).
Buckets are Pool/0/<id // 2048>/<id % 2048>.bucket (~50 MiB) with .index and .lock beside them; a 3 TB target is about a million files, most of them small dedup index files under Config/@cand_file.
Each database is kept twice (name and name_dup); a _dup copy is read when the main one is unreadable.
todo: single-version and cloud targets are untested

formats.name: Thunderbird profile copy by ImportExportTools NG

detection.description: A <profile with . as _>-<yyyymmdd>-<hhmm> folder (or a fixed custom name) written by the add-on's profile backup.

metadata_read.Backup.log: backup date and every saved file by its original path (the manifest), copy errors
metadata_read.prefs.js: each mail account (mail.server.serverN): name, type, host, folder, message store (mbox or maildir)
metadata_read.layout: per account from the listing: mbox folders (a file beside its .msf) and bytes, maildir message files; the host from maildir file names

problems: files Backup.log saved that are not in the copy
files in a dated copy the log does not name
the log's copy errors
notes: Each run is a full plain copy of the profile, so generations are near duplicates; `filecat dupes` ignores clusters made only of backup data (--include-backups shows them).
The log has no sizes, checksums or end marker: presence is all that can be checked, and a run cut short looks like a smaller backup.
The add-on copies one file every 50 ms while Thunderbird runs: about 18 h for 480 000 files, so the copy is not a single point in time.
With a fixed custom folder name it copies only files changed since the last run, so files the log does not name are expected and not reported.

One profile can mix stores: each account is mbox (one file per folder, beside its .msf index; subfolders in <folder>.sbd/) or maildir (<folder>/cur/<message>.eml). The profile examined had two mbox accounts and four maildir ones.
todo: messages inside mbox folders are not counted (that needs reading them: one 'From ' line each)
zip backups made by the add-on's manual export are not recognised

formats.name: Veeam backup job folder (.vbm / .vbk / .vib / .vrb)

detection.description: A Veeam Agent (Windows / Linux) or Backup & Replication job folder: the .vbm and one file per restore point. Without a .vbm only Veeam's timestamped file names count, so VMware .vib bundles and dictionary .vrb files are not taken for one.

metadata_read.<job>.vbm: job name and ids, where it was written, encryption; every backup file with its time, BackupSize and DataSize; restore points with type, chain link, corrupt / consistent flags; machine name, BIOS UUID, OS and disks

actions.verify_flag: --verify-backups (reads each backup file's header, snapshot slots and metadata banks, ~0.02% of it, and checks their CRC32C and end-of-file; data blocks are not read)

formats.copy_keys: veeam-point:<restore point id> of each point on disk and not corrupt
problems: backup files the .vbm lists that are missing or of another size
restore points Veeam marked corrupt, partial increments, increments whose parent is not listed (with the number of later points that depend on a missing or corrupt one)
backup files in the folder the .vbm does not list
with --verify-backups: files without a valid snapshot slot, truncated files, metadata banks that fail their checksum
notes: Veeam does not document the format; the layout was read from Veeam Agent for Windows jobs (storage format 13, .vbm Version 22-5140).
BackupSize in the .vbm is the backup file's size in bytes; a point that never finished is marked IsCorrupted with BackupSize 0.
The .vbm keeps the path Veeam wrote to (DirPath, Storage FilePath); files are matched by name, so a moved job folder still checks.
todo: Backup & Replication per-machine chains (several .vbm per folder), reverse increments (.vrb) and log backups (.vlb) are untested

formats.name: Synology Active Backup for Google Workspace task

detection.description: ActiveBackupForGoogleWorkspace/task_<n> on an Active Backup for Business share: one folder per user plus the databases.

measured_normally: <user>/MyDrive/** (the latest copy of each Drive file, under its own name)

metadata_read.task-config.sqlite: task name, domain, admin, backup policy, retention (named fields only: it also holds an encrypted private key)
metadata_read.account.sqlite: every user: id, name, email, status, folder, used bytes per service, enabled services (named fields only: it also holds OAuth tokens)
metadata_read.service-log.sqlite, <service>-log.sqlite: runs: count, first and last, each user's latest run per service with its log text
metadata_read.<user id>/mail.sqlite, calendar-event.sq: every item version, checked against the walk's listing

actions.verify_flag: --verify-backups (reads every META and Drive .metadata and checks the size and MD5 of what they name)

problems: message, event or contact versions with no folder or no META (or SKEL) fragment
item folders no database lists
MyDrive files with no version in #SynoVersionRepo, or of another size than the latest
an active user's latest run of an enabled service that failed
with --verify-backups: fragments and versions missing or whose size or MD5 differs from their metadata
notes: Synology does not document the layout; it was read from an ABG task with 50 users (task-config version 13).
Every message is its own folder of 2-4 small files, so a large mailbox is hundreds of thousands of files; listing them is the whole cost of a default scan.
Items deleted in Google keep their folders; their rows get an end_time instead of 4294967295.
A task backs up every few minutes, so items newer than every item the listing found are counted as backed up after the listing, not as missing.
Calendar event folders are often past MAX_PATH on Windows; a service with missing items that long is listed again with \\?\ paths before they are reported.
todo: shared drives (team-drive.sqlite) are untested: none in the task examined
the hash that picks the two <xx>/<yy> bucket folders is unknown
Active Backup for Microsoft 365 (ActiveBackupForMicrosoft365/task_<n>, @ActiveBackupOffice365-Databases) looks the same and is not handled yet

formats.name: Windows Backup and Restore file backup

detection.description: A <COMPUTER> folder holding Backup Set folders.

problems: missing Backup files N.zip
zip without its Catalogs/Backup files N.wbcat
Catalogs/GlobalCatalog.wbcat missing
notes: The .wbcat catalog format is not public; checks come from the layout.

formats.name: Windows system image (WindowsImageBackup)
problems: Catalog folder missing
Backup folder without a .vhd/.vhdx

formats.name: duplicity / deja-dup target

detection.description: A folder of duplicity set files.

metadata_read.*.manifest: Hostname, Localdir and the volume list (unencrypted manifests only)

problems: set without a manifest (did not finish)
missing signatures
volume gaps or volumes the manifest lists that are missing
incremental set that continues no chain
notes: Encrypted (.gpg) manifests are not read.

archives.name: 7-Zip archive
archives.magic: offset 0: 37 7A BC AF 27 1C ('7z' BC AF 27 1C), then format version major.minor
archives.reads: The 32-byte start header, then the header database at 32 + NextHeaderOffset (the end of the file). Never a member's packed bytes.

metadata_read.start header: version, next-header offset/size/CRC; start and header CRC mismatches are recorded
metadata_read.encoded header: inflated when the one coder is Copy, LZMA or LZMA2 (the 7-Zip default); capped at 128 MiB
metadata_read.files info: names (UTF-16), empty-stream / empty-file / directory flags, modified times, attributes
metadata_read.streams info: folders (solid blocks), coders, packed sizes, per-file unpack sizes and CRC32s

probe_keys: probe.7z.{version, folders, packed_size, methods, solid, expected_size, header_encoded, header_encrypted, encrypted}
problems: header ends past the end of the file (incomplete download, or a .7z.001 first volume): probe.truncated and an error, no members
start header or header CRC mismatch: probe.7z.start_header_crc_ok / header_crc_ok = false
encrypted header: probe.7z.header_encrypted, members not listed
header coder other than Copy/LZMA/LZMA2: error recorded, members not listed
notes: Packed size is per folder, not per file: a solid archive has no per-member compressed size.
A self-extracting .exe is a PE and is handled by the PE probe, not this one.
Checked on the 269 MB Cisco-IOU-L2-L3-Collection-v2.7z: one solid LZMA folder, 28 members, header length matches the file size exactly.

archives.name: ZIP archive (and the formats built on it)
archives.reads: The end-of-central-directory record and the central directory (zipfile.ZipFile on open). Never a local header or member data.
notes: A first entry named [Content_Types].xml makes it kind=document (Office Open XML); container stays zip.
Only the local-header magic is sniffed: an empty ZIP (PK 05 06) and a spanned ZIP (PK 07 08) are not detected.
Times: the 0x5455 extended timestamp when present, otherwise DOS time read as UTC.

archives.name: gzip (and the XOR-wrapped gzip used by X3 .pck/.dat)
archives.magic: offset 0: 1F 8B; or those two bytes (and the method byte) xor one key byte (gzip_xored)
archives.reads: Inflates up to 4 MiB (GZIP_PROBE_CAP) to classify the content; if it is a tar, streams the tar up to archive_scan_cap, or to the end with --deep-archives.
member_fields: tar members only: see the tar entry
probe_keys: probe.gzip.{method, flags, mtime, os, original_name, original_size}
notes: original_size is the gzip ISIZE field: the size modulo 2**32, ambiguous above 4 GiB.
A gzip that is not a tar lists no members; kind comes from the inflated bytes (text, image, ...).

archives.name: bzip2
archives.spec: https://sourceware.org/bzip2/ (libbzip2 source; there is no formal specification)
archives.reads: As gzip: classify the first 4 MiB inflated, list an embedded tar.
member_fields: tar members only: see the tar entry
notes: bzip2 carries no uncompressed size, so none is reported without decompressing the whole stream.
The old bzip1 format (magic BZ0) is not recognised.

archives.name: xz
archives.reads: The stream footer and index for sizes; then as gzip for classification and an embedded tar.
member_fields: tar members only: see the tar entry
notes: The size comes from the index without decompressing anything.
A .raw-disk-image.xz / .img.xz is not unpacked to look at the disk inside.

archives.name: tar (ustar, GNU, PAX, old V7)
archives.dispatch: filecat.probe._probe, step 5b; walk() is also used for tars inside gzip/bzip2/xz
archives.magic: offset 257: 'ustar' NUL or 'ustar  ' NUL; V7 tar has no magic and is accepted only when the header checksum validates
archives.reads: 512-byte headers, seeking past member data. GNU long name/link (L, K), PAX extended headers (x, g) and base-256 sizes are handled.
probe_keys: probe.scan_stopped_at (a compressed tar stopped at the cap)
notes: Compressed tars are listed for gzip, bzip2 and xz only; zstd, lzma, lz4, lzip, lzop, brotli and .Z tars are identified by name but not unpacked.
docs/TODO.md: an .ova is a tar whose first member is an .ovf; not yet read.

archives.name: MPQ (Blizzard MoPaQ)
archives.magic: offset 0: 'MPQ' 1A (archive header) or 'MPQ' 1B (user-data header that points at the archive header)
archives.reads: The header (v1-v4), the encrypted hash and block tables, and the (listfile) member only.
probe_keys: probe.mpq.{format_version, sector_size, archive_size, hash_table_entries, block_table_entries, unnamed_blocks, listfile}
problems: no (listfile): members are listed as <block N>, names unknown
(listfile) names that are not in the hash table are listed with an error
notes: Blocks the (listfile) does not name are counted in probe.mpq.unnamed_blocks.

archives.name: Godot resource pack (.pck)
notes: Several unrelated formats use .pck (X3 gzip packs, Python pickles); the bytes decide, see probe/pck.py.

archives.name: ISO 9660 / UDF discs, SquashFS, and virtual or raw disk images
archives.magic: 'QFI' FB (qcow2), 'conectix' (VHD), 'vhdxfile' (VHDX), 'KDMV' (VMDK), 0xBEDA107F (VDI), plus ISO 9660 / UDF volume descriptors and 'hsqs' (SquashFS)
archives.spec: https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-119/ (ISO 9660); https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-167/ (ECMA-167, the base of UDF; OSTA's UDF 2.60 spec is osta.org/specs); https://dr-emann.github.io/squashfs/ (SquashFS)
archives.reads: Headers, a few sectors and mapping tables with targeted seeks; partitions become member rows (role volume) and ISO files become member rows by name.
probe_keys: see probe/disk.py and file-catalog-requirements.md, Probe order step 4b
notes: Listed here because freedesktop files SquashFS and compressed ISOs with the archives; the detail lives in probe/disk.py.

archives_identified_only.name: RAR
archives_identified_only.notes: Kind stays unknown (name and MIME only). RAR4 and RAR5 differ; multi-volume sets are *.partN.rar or *.r00. Header-encrypted archives hide the file names.

archives_identified_only.name: Microsoft Cabinet
archives_identified_only.notes: Windows Update (.msu) and installers. The CFFOLDER/CFFILE index at the front is cheap to read: a good next candidate.

archives_identified_only.name: Windows Installer package / patch (OLE compound)
archives_identified_only.magic: offset 0: D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1 (OLE); the class id in the directory tells msi from other OLE files
archives_identified_only.notes: Not an archive structure to list; product name and version are in the SummaryInformation stream.

archives_identified_only.name: Windows Imaging (WIM / SWM)
archives_identified_only.notes: Install media and deployment images. An XML block names the images, editions and sizes; one read would do.

archives_identified_only.name: Zstandard
archives_identified_only.notes: The frame header can carry the content size. A .tar.zst is not unpacked (Python has no zstd before 3.14). Used by pacman packages and many backup tools.

archives_identified_only.name: LZ4 frame
archives_identified_only.notes: Content size is optional in the frame header.

archives_identified_only.name: LZMA (.lzma, LZMA_Alone)
archives_identified_only.magic: offset 0: 5D, then an 8-byte size field (often all FF)
archives_identified_only.notes: The magic is a single byte, so the name decides. Python's lzma.FORMAT_ALONE can read it.

archives_identified_only.name: lzip
archives_identified_only.notes: The trailer carries the data size and CRC.

archives_identified_only.name: UNIX compress (.Z)
archives_identified_only.notes: Legacy; seen in old software mirrors.

archives_identified_only.name: Brotli
archives_identified_only.magic: none reliable (freedesktop lists CE B2 CF 81 for the framed form)
archives_identified_only.notes: Raw Brotli has no magic, so only the name identifies it.

archives_identified_only.name: bzip3
archives_identified_only.notes: Newer than bzip2 and unrelated to it.

archives_identified_only.name: lzop
archives_identified_only.notes: Fast compressor used in some backup scripts.

archives_identified_only.name: cpio (odc, newc, newc+CRC, binary)
archives_identified_only.notes: Linux initramfs images and RPM payloads are cpio; a good candidate beside tar since the walk has the same shape.

archives_identified_only.name: ar archive (static libraries, Debian packages)
archives_identified_only.notes: A .deb is an ar holding debian-binary, control.tar.* and data.tar.*.

archives_identified_only.name: RPM package
archives_identified_only.notes: The header section carries name, version and architecture; the payload is a compressed cpio.

archives_identified_only.name: XAR (eXtensible ARchive, macOS .pkg)
archives_identified_only.notes: A header plus a zlib-compressed XML table of contents that lists every member, so it can be listed cheaply.

archives_identified_only.name: ARJ
archives_identified_only.spec: ARJ technical information file (ARJ source distribution)
archives_identified_only.notes: DOS-era; names sit in a chain of local headers.

archives_identified_only.name: LHA / LZH
archives_identified_only.notes: Common in Japanese software and Amiga collections.

archives_identified_only.name: ACE
archives_identified_only.notes: Proprietary; extraction tools are scarce and old ones had unsafe path handling.

archives_identified_only.name: ALZip
archives_identified_only.notes: Korean ALZip format.

archives_identified_only.name: Zoo
archives_identified_only.notes: DOS/Unix era.

archives_identified_only.name: ARC (SEA)
archives_identified_only.notes: freedesktop lists no extension; the magic is weak.

archives_identified_only.name: StuffIt / StuffIt X
archives_identified_only.notes: Classic Mac OS archives.

archives_identified_only.name: ZPAQ journaling archive
archives_identified_only.notes: Backup-style: each update appends a version, so one file holds a history.

archives_identified_only.name: DAR (Disk ARchive)
archives_identified_only.notes: Backup tool; archives are split into numbered slices <name>.<N>.dar. Belongs with the backup formats if it is added.

archives_identified_only.name: qpress
archives_identified_only.notes: What xtrabackup --compress writes; see the planned xtrabackup entry.

archives_identified_only.name: rzip / lrzip
archives_identified_only.notes: Long-range-redundancy compressors for very large files.

archives_identified_only.name: Parchive (PAR2)
archives_identified_only.notes: Repair data for another set of files, not an archive of them; the set's names and sizes are in the main packet. Usually sits beside a split archive.

archives_identified_only.name: Git bundle
archives_identified_only.magic: offset 0: '# v2 git bundle' or '# v3 git bundle' LF
archives_identified_only.notes: A repository backup: a text header lists prerequisites and refs, then a pack follows. Cheap to read.

archives_identified_only.name: Flatpak bundle
archives_identified_only.notes: An OSTree commit wrapped as a single file.

archives_identified_only.name: Alpine Package Keeper package
archives_identified_only.notes: Shares *.apk with Android packages; the Android one is a ZIP, so the bytes tell them apart.

archives_identified_only.name: Doom WAD
archives_identified_only.notes: Game asset container with a flat lump directory; the same family as MPQ and PCK.

archives_identified_only.name: Partially downloaded file
archives_identified_only.notes: Not an archive: browser temp files. Worth flagging in a catalog because the real file is incomplete.
